title: Pinned model handshake: change-matrix, IO invariants, and rollback hooks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Define a compact, machine-readable 'change-matrix' and accompanying IO invariants for pinned model versions so that: (1) engineering can automatically gate incompatible rollouts, (2) product/SDK clients get deterministic guarantees about prompt/output shapes, and (3) the Console can publish a clear performance+compatibility profile for each pinned model.

Scope:
- Design a change-matrix that maps classes of model/API change -> allowed/forbidden rollout actions and required migration steps. Change classes include: tokenizer changes, output shape/schema changes (fields removed/added/renamed), deterministic behavior shifts (sampling defaults), new structured output types (JSON schemas), latency/throughput performance regressions, and safety-filter changes.
- Define strict IO invariants: required fields (prompt->response), optional metadata, stable sampling parameter ranges, and canonicalized tokenizer expectations.
- Define thresholds and signals to detect semantic/regression divergence using: eval prompt set + embedding distance checks, deterministic unit tests, and sample-based BLEU/ROUGE/style drift metrics.
- Publish a 'compatibility manifest' artifact for every pinned model version in the model catalog: JSON with fields for IO-schema, tokenizer-hash, allowed-parameter-range, perf-profile (p50/p95 latencies, tokens/sec), known-incompatibilities, and recommended migration steps.
- Implement automatic rollback hooks: when a rollout to pinned model vX triggers predefined regression signals (high semantic drift on core prompt set or latency above SLA), the system will automatically fall back to previous pinned version and emit an incident with suggested remediation.
- Add console surfaces: per-model change-matrix view, clear flags for 'breaking' vs 'non-breaking' model updates, and a downloadable compatibility manifest.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Change-matrix schema defined and documented in Confluence; reviewed and approved by PM and Design.
2) Compatibility manifest produced by onboarding pipeline for new pinned versions and uploaded to the model catalog on successful onboarding.
3) Rollout engine consumes change-matrix to block canary rollouts of changes marked as 'breaking' unless an explicit override is provided with risk justification.
4) Automatic rollback triggers validated in integration tests: at least two synthetic regression scenarios cause rollback and create incident artifacts.
5) Console shows per-model compatibility manifest and flags in the model detail page; UX copy reviewed.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Draft change-matrix schema and compatibility-manifest JSON schema; gather PM/design feedback. (Owner: Luca)
- Week 2: Implement manifest generation in onboarding pipeline; add tokenizer hashing and schema extraction. (Owner: infra-team)
- Week 3: Integrate change-matrix evaluation into rollout engine; add simple auto-rollback hook. (Owner: runtime-team)
- Week 4: Add integration tests, perf smoke tests, and Console surfaces; finalize docs and release notes.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for manifest serialization, tokenizer hash detection, and schema diffing.
- Regression harness that runs curated prompt set against 'previous' and 'candidate' pinned versions and checks embedding cosine distance thresholds, structural schema diffs, and sampling-based divergence scores.
- Load/perf tests to ensure manifest generation and change evaluation do not add >5% latency to onboarding pipeline.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONBOARD/Change+Matrix+Spec (draft)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/1234 (PoC manifest generator)
- Perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/model-onboard/perf-suite (smoke runs)

Notes / trade-offs:
- We intentionally keep the change-matrix compact rather than attempting to capture semantic equivalence fully. Full semantic compatibility is undecidable; we instead provide a conservative gate plus a clear override path for emergency upgrades.
- Tokenizer hash mismatches are considered breaking by default; small tokenizer merges (e.g., adding unused special tokens) can be allowed if explicitly annotated in the manifest.
- Sampling default changes are categorized as 'risky' but can be rolled out behind deterministic flags.

Deliverables:
- change-matrix schema PR merged
- manifest generator and sample manifests for 3 models
- rollout engine integration and auto-rollback demo
- Console compatibility page with downloadable manifest

Longer-term: tie compatibility signals into Redwood Optimize so model quantization or kernel selection recommendations maintain manifest invariants and automatically produce compatibility notes in the manifest.
